name: Winter Olympics

milestones.title: It begins in Chamonix
milestones.text: The competition later recognised as the first Olympic Winter Games brings 258 athletes to the French Alps. Women compete in figure skating.

milestones.title: Two absent editions
milestones.text: World War II interrupts the Games. The timeline leaves both editions empty; winter competition resumes at St. Moritz in 1948.

milestones.title: A first for Asia
milestones.text: Sapporo becomes the first Winter Olympic host outside Europe and North America.

milestones.title: A rhythm of its own
milestones.text: Lillehammer follows Albertville by two years as the Winter Games move to a separate cycle from the Summer Games.

milestones.title: A wider programme
milestones.text: Nagano introduces snowboarding and women’s ice hockey. Curling returns to the medal programme.

milestones.title: Milano Cortina
milestones.text: Ski mountaineering joins the programme. Johannes Høsflot Klæbo wins all six men’s cross-country skiing events, taking his career gold count to eleven.

notes: 25 held Winter Games, 1924–2026; 1,278 events with medal awards, across 17 discipline labels including military patrol in 1924. The source also lists the abandoned 1928 speed skating 10,000 m event; it is retained as a cancelled event and is excluded from medal-event counts. The 1940 and 1944 Games were cancelled.

3,849 event-level medal awards. A team, pair or relay counts once in a nation’s table, regardless of roster size. Tied medals remain separate awards, including ties between competitors from the same nation. Rankings sort by gold, then silver, then bronze; exact ties share a rank. Athlete views count listed medal-roster appearances, including named alternates where the source includes them. These roster lists may be incomplete or use name variants; they are not an independently certified individual medal register.

All 25 edition medal tables were reconciled country by country and medal colour by medal colour, with one deliberate exclusion: the special 1924 alpinism gold for the Everest expedition is outside this competition-event atlas. Demonstration events, the Paralympics, Youth Games and winter sports held at the 1908/1920 Summer Olympics are outside scope. No times, scores, participation rates or full finishing orders are implied.

Historical delegations remain separate: Soviet Union, Unified Team, East Germany, West Germany, United Team of Germany, Russia, Olympic Athletes from Russia, ROC and Individual Neutral Athletes are not combined. Czech Republic and Czechia use the single display name Czechia. The sport filter uses discipline names, not the IOC’s broader sport grouping. “Open” identifies pre-2026 luge doubles; “Mixed” includes pairs and mixed-team competitions.

method: Every medal event of every Winter Games, read from Wikipedia’s list of medal winners for that Games at the recorded revision: the event and its sport, the men’s, women’s, mixed or open category, and the gold, silver and bronze awards with the delegation and the athletes the list names. A team, pair or relay counts once in a delegation’s table; ties are separate awards; the medal table of every Games reconciles by delegation and colour against the cited comparison table. Demonstration events are outside the archive. Host cities are placed on the Natural Earth land silhouette at approximate coordinates.
